subject: Re: Acme Corp TCO discussion — token economics & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have clear next steps. I’ve attached a simple TCO model (acme_tco_model.xlsx) and our pricing options PDF.

Pain points you called out:
- Token spend is growing quickly (you estimated ~200M tokens/month across search + chat).
- Cost unpredictability from bursty patterns and varied prompt lengths.
- Need to keep latency under 400ms p95 for chat flows.
- Tight procurement budget for FY26: target external inference spend ~ $20k–$30k/month.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce per-token cost and stabilize monthly spend (predictable committed spend).
- Preserve quality for customer-facing chat (no more than a 5% drop in satisfaction).
- Get a pilot in prod for one vertical (support chat) within 8 weeks.

Cost / TCO levers we discussed (high-level):
- Model choice: smaller/quantized variants for non-customer-facing workloads and higher-quality variants for chat.
- Batching: request-level batching for high-throughput inference (best for embeddings/rerank).
- KV/prefix caching: for chat conversations with repeat contexts, we can reduce repeated decode work.
- Quantization & kernel selection: 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants can reduce GPU cost materially on Dedicated.
- Routing: mix hosted + dedicated to keep predictable capacity for critical routes while using hosted for bursty traffic.

Initial TCO sketch (very rough):
- Baseline (current): ~200M tokens/mo at your current provider -> ~ $X (we’ll calculate exact baseline from your invoices).
- With batching + caching + mixed routing: estimated 2–3x effective token reduction on cost-sensitive workloads.
- Example: if we convert 60% of traffic to cached/batched paths + quantized models, unit token cost could drop by ~50–70% for that portion.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share last 3 months of token invoices/usage (we’ll use them in the attached TCO model).
2) Redwood will run a short workload analysis and return a detailed TCO with 3 scenarios (hosted-only, dedicated-reserved, hybrid) — deliverable in 5 business days.
3) Technical deep-dive with Dylan to validate latency/kv cache expectations (target dates below).
4) Procurement: draft MSA + commitment options from Rishi for Acme’s budget envelope.

Proposed call slots for the technical deep-dive:
- Tue 5/18 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu 5/20 13:00–14:00 PT

Attachments: acme_tco_model.xlsx (TCO model stub), redwood_pricing_options.pdf

Appreciate the partnership — I’ll coordinate the model run once you share usage data.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Acme - post-call TCO recap & next steps

Alex — nice to meet you (virtually). Attaching our pricing options doc and a short note on where the biggest wins come from. High level:

1) Hosted (pay-as-you-go) — fastest to start, good for bursty/experimental workloads. Unit token cost higher but operational overhead low.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — best for predictable, high-volume production workloads (embeddings & batching benefit a lot). Lower unit cost when you commit.
3) Hybrid — pin mission-critical chat to Dedicated, keep analytics/batch on Hosted to absorb spikes.

Quantification example (order-of-magnitude illustrative):
- Hosted baseline unit: $0.0025 per 1k tokens (example ballpark)
- Dedicated (reserved + quantized paths): effective unit ~ $0.0009–0.0012 per 1k tokens depending on commit level & quantization
- Combined effect with batch + cache: realized spend on eligible traffic can be 40–60% lower versus hosted baseline for those flows.

We’ll tailor these numbers after we run your usage through Marissa’s model. Security: our standard MSA + SOC2 report and private deployment options (VPC) are available if you need them; I’ll loop in our security lead once you confirm.

Action items I’ll own:
- Provide commitment tiers and sample contract language for a $20k–$30k/month envelope.
- Deliver a simple comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid) after Marissa runs the usage file.

Attached: redwood_pricing_options.pdf

Thanks — Rishi
VP, Solutions & Pricing
Redwood Inference
